how do I tell if a graph is 2 colorable? Be brief

* A graph is 2-colorable if and only if it is bipartite.
* Use BFS or DFS to attempt to color the graph with 2 colors.
* Start by assigning color 0 to any vertex.
* Assign the opposite color (1 - current color) to all adjacent vertices.
* If an adjacent vertex already has the same color as the current vertex, the graph is not 2-colorable.
* If the algorithm completes without conflicts, the graph is 2-colorable.
* A graph is bipartite if and only if it contains no odd-length cycles.
* You can also check for odd cycles directly by detecting if any cycle has an odd number of edges.
* The time complexity of this check is O(V + E), where V is vertices and E is edges.
